title: Give (or take back) Invardia support access to a PIM Manager installation
purpose: Gives (or with -Remove takes back) the customer's Invardia Support app its access to this PIM Manager installation: its own read-only database user (the read role pim_support_read) and the time-limited support access module with the level as the consent (troubleshoot = read only; setup = admin rights only inside an open support session, at most 8 hours); asbuilt = start the as-built job (caj-pim-asbuilt) and read the PDFs it writes (troubleshoot and setup include it). The Support app is never made a member of the SQL admin group, never a database owner and never an owner of PIM's app registrations or groups. Every change is read back.
whenToRun: When the customer wants Invardia support to look at (troubleshoot) or repair (setup) their installation, and to take that access back afterwards (-Remove). The guided public install runs it for you when a support app is named. For a private installation, run it from inside the network (the SQL server has no public endpoint). It is part of the PIM Manager release package, not a separate download: run it from the package folder that Install-Invardia (or the guided install) downloaded and verified (.\tools\setup\Grant-PimSupportAccess.ps1). Invardia's New-InvardiaSupportApp.ps1 must have created the support app in the tenant first.

runAs.name: Member of the environment's SQL admin group (grp-pim-sql-admins) or the server's Entra admin, signed in through the browser or the Invardia Support app session (no Azure CLI)
runAs.why: Creates the support app's read-only database user, installs the time-limited support access module (the read role, the consent, the signed procedures) and reads it back; with -Remove drops the user.

runAs.name: Privileged Role Administrator
runAs.scope: the tenant (only for -Remove, where an earlier grant made the support app a member of the SQL admin group)
runAs.why: The SQL admin group is role-assignable: removing a member needs this role. Without it that part is reported and the rest continues (exit 1).

runAs.name: Owner of PIM's app registrations and groups (or Application Administrator / Groups Administrator)
runAs.scope: PIM's own objects in the tenant (only for -Remove, where an earlier grant made the support app an owner)
runAs.why: Removes the support app as an owner of the Manager's sign-in app, the access request API app, the Manager members group and the SQL admin group.

runAs.name: Reader
runAs.scope: the PIM resource group (only when -SqlServer is not given)
runAs.why: Finds the PIM SQL server in -ResourceGroup.

runAs.name: User Access Administrator
runAs.scope: the PIM resource group (only for the as-built access: -Level asbuilt / troubleshoot / setup / -Remove with -SubscriptionId and -ResourceGroup)
runAs.why: Creates the custom Azure role 'PIM Manager as-built runner' (Owner works too) and assigns it plus Storage Blob Data Reader to the support app. Role Based Access Control Administrator is enough once the role exists (Deploy-PimAsBuiltJob creates it).

changes.object: the support app's own database user, created from the application's client id as a SID (never FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER) when no user has that id -- named [invardia-support]; an existing user of the support app is reused whatever its name
changes.permission: the read role pim_support_read only (SELECT on the product schemas pim and platform) -- the ONE standing database right, at every level
changes.why: Invardia support reads the store to troubleshoot. No db_owner, no db_datareader and no VIEW DEFINITION are given.
changes.undo: Run the script with -Remove (drops the user), or switch the Invardia Support app off in Microsoft Entra ID.

changes.object: the time-limited support access module: the schema pimsupport (the consent and the grant records), the read role pim_support_read, three signed procedures (open, close, state)
changes.permission: the consent level: troubleshoot (troubleshoot and asbuilt) = read only; setup = admin rights (db_owner) only inside an open support session, at most 8 hours, closed by the installation's own support job
changes.why: Admin rights for a repair exist only for the length of a support session, never as a standing right.
changes.undo: Run the script with -Remove (drops the support app's user; its rights go with it).

changes.object: the custom role 'PIM Manager as-built runner (<resource group>)' when it does not exist yet: Microsoft.App/jobs/start/action + Microsoft.App/jobs/executions/read, assignable in the PIM resource group
changes.why: The narrowest right to start the as-built job and follow its execution -- no job read, no logs, no secrets, no stop.
changes.undo: Delete the role definition after its assignments are removed.

changes.object: the support app's service principal (as-built document, PIM 100.61)
changes.permission: the custom role 'PIM Manager as-built runner' (start the job + read its executions)
changes.why: -Level asbuilt (included in troubleshoot and setup): Invardia support starts the as-built job on request.
changes.undo: Run the script with -Remove (deletes the assignment).

changes.object: the support app's service principal (as-built document, PIM 100.61)
changes.scope: the ONE container 'asbuilt' of the PIM storage account (the PDFs are deleted after 1 day)
changes.why: Invardia support reads the PDF the job wrote, for that occasion, and stores nothing.
changes.undo: Run the script with -Remove (deletes the assignment).

changes.target: Microsoft Entra ID, the SQL database and Azure RBAC
changes.object: the database user (with every role it holds), a membership of the SQL admin group and owner entries on PIM's app registrations and groups that an earlier version gave, and the as-built role assignments (only with -Remove)

parameters.name: AppId
parameters.help: The Invardia Support app's application (client) id in this tenant.

parameters.name: Level
parameters.help: troubleshoot (read-only database user + the as-built access), setup (the same, and admin rights only inside an open support session of at most 8 hours) or asbuilt (start the as-built job and read its PDFs; with -SqlServer also the read-only database user).

parameters.name: TenantId
parameters.help: The tenant id. Every token is pinned to it.

parameters.name: SubscriptionId
parameters.help: The PIM subscription (used to find the SQL server when -SqlServer is not given).

parameters.name: ResourceGroup
parameters.help: The PIM resource group (used to find the SQL server when -SqlServer is not given).

parameters.name: EnvLabel
parameters.help: The per-environment label the deploy used (-EnvLabel), so the right app registrations and groups are found.

parameters.name: SqlAdminGroupName
parameters.help: The SQL admin group's name (read to report an earlier membership; -Remove takes it back).

parameters.name: AsBuiltJobName
parameters.help: The as-built job (Deploy-PimAsBuiltJob.ps1); the storage account it names in PIM_ASBUILT_STORAGE is where the container asbuilt is granted.

parameters.name: Remove
parameters.help: Take back everything: the database user, a membership and owner entries an earlier version gave, and the as-built role assignments.

readsOnly: the support app's service principal, the SQL admin group's members, and with -Remove PIM's app registrations and groups and their owners (Microsoft Graph)
the SQL servers in -ResourceGroup (only when -SqlServer is not given)
the support app's database user by its id and its roles, and the support access module's state (read-back)
the as-built job (the storage account it names) and the support app's role assignments on that job and on the container asbuilt
network: management.azure.com (to find the SQL server, and the as-built role assignments)
whatIf: Reads the support app and the SQL admin group and prints 'What if: Performing the operation "the Support app's own database user (from its client id) in pim_support_read only, and the support access module with consent '<level>'" on target ...' and the as-built grants it would make, then 'preview only -- nothing was changed'. Nothing is written.
undo: Run the script again with -Remove: it drops the database user and takes back a membership, every owner entry and the as-built role assignments.
